## Shell Terminal Panel [⌘⇧S]{.kbd} {#shell .i-terminal}

::: {.layout .layout-page}
::: {.fig data-figure="layout-shell" aria-label="Emaki's window with the Shell Terminal Panel shown in color at the chat's right: its tabs, prompts and output. The rest is gray. The panel stands forward under the pointer, and its button in the chrome puts it away."}
:::
:::

Opening a terminal and `cd`-ing to the project is easy, but doing it
again and again is a pain. Emaki solves it for you! The Shell Terminal Panel gives you terminal tabs that open in the project's folder. Use the **+** button or [⌘T]{.kbd} to open a new tab, and [⌘W]{.kbd} to close one. Inside the terminal, you can use your mouse, scrolling, and keyboard shortcuts.

Its look is inspired by [Kaku](https://kaku.fun), in the window's own colors and font.

## Agent Terminal Panel [⌘⇧A]{.kbd} {#agent .i-sparkles}

::: {.layout .layout-page}
::: {.fig data-figure="layout-agent" aria-label="Emaki's window with the Agent Terminal Panel shown in color at the chat's right: the agent's own screen. The rest is gray. The panel stands forward under the pointer, and its button in the chrome puts it away."}
:::
:::

If you want your agent's original CLI, this is the right panel. You can use it as a fallback, or even continue your session in it. As in the Shell Terminal Panel, you can use your mouse, scrolling, and keyboard shortcuts.
